structure: Part 11, the notification hub: the four traces of journeys.fit.spec.js › the notification hub, each opened and mined in full (actions, network log, snapshots). (1) journeys--the-notification-hub-a-fresh-notification-lists-every-task-as-to-do (59 actions): create-notification 302 to notification-type, live-animals chosen, Continue lands on origin-of-the-import, then a direct navigate to /design-release-2.1/notification-hub; snapshot at action 37 is the fresh hub. (2) journeys--the-notification-hub-a-hub-task-link-returns-to-the-hub-after-saving (33 actions): fresh hub, click 'Main import reason' to /reason-for-import?from=hub (snapshot action 16), choose Re-entry, Save and continue, back on the hub with that task 'Complete' (snapshot action 20). (3) journeys--the-notification-hub-review-with-tasks-missing-lists-each-incomplete-section (63 actions): origin (France, no region), what-are-you-importing (cattle, Bos Taurus), reason (Internal market, Breeding), consignment-details (1 animal), then a direct navigate to /review-notification (snapshot action 37 to 47) and Continue, which re-renders the review (snapshot action 50). (4) journeys--the-notification-hub-the-submitted-page-is-guarded-until-the-declaration-is-confirmed (27 actions): a fresh notification, direct navigate to /notification-submitted, 302 to /declaration (snapshot action 14). Pages covered, in journey order: the hub ('Overview', always shown once a notification exists), one hub task page as entered from the hub (Main import reason, with from=hub), the review page in its incomplete state, and the declaration page reached through the submitted-page guard. The intermediate question pages walked in trace 3 belong to other parts and are claimed here only as they show on the hub and review. Not reached in this slice, recorded as gaps: an 'In progress' or other task status, the 'Save and return to overview' button, clicking 'Review and submit' or 'Return to dashboard', the Delete flow, the declaration's unchecked-box error, and the submitted page itself.

claims.statement: Starting a notification at /design-release-2.1/create-notification redirects to the notification type page.
Choosing live animals as the notification type and continuing takes the user to the origin page, not to the hub.
The notification hub lives at /design-release-2.1/notification-hub and can be opened directly once a notification has been started.
The hub's page title is 'Overview - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
The hub's main heading is 'Overview'.
Above the heading, the hub shows the notification's status as a 'Draft' tag while it has not been submitted.
Beside the status tag, the hub shows the notification's reference, which already exists for a fresh notification before any task is answered.

A live-animals notification reference takes the form GBN-AG-, a two-digit year, a hyphen and six upper-case letters or digits: three traces show GBN-AG-26-0BEJ1Y, GBN-AG-26-05GIU6 and GBN-AG-26-0M2F7E.
claims.ref: trace journeys--the-notification-hub-a-fresh-notification-lists-every-task-as-to-do action 37; trace journeys--the-notification-hub-a-hub-task-link-returns-to-the-hub-after-saving action 16; trace journeys--the-notification-hub-review-with-tasks-missing-lists-each-incomplete-section action 37
claims.note: The format is inferred from three examples, all generated in 2026; whether 26 is the year is an inference.

claims.statement: The hub's task list is built from custom app-notification-hub-* markup (sections with h3 headings and a list of link plus tag rows) rather than the GOV.UK Task list component, though it uses govuk-link, govuk-tag and govuk-button inside it; the GOV.UK Task list component, with its status tags and hint support, could replace it.
The commodities totals are custom app-notification-hub-card tiles (a large value, a label and a caption), a pattern with no direct GOV.UK Frontend component.
The status and reference strip above the heading is custom (app-dr2-notification-status), with a govuk-tag restyled by app-dr2-review-status__tag--draft.
Clicking a hub task link opens that task's page with from=hub in the URL; clicking 'Main import reason' opens /design-release-2.1/reason-for-import?from=hub.
A task page opened from the hub carries the hub origin through the form as a hidden field from=hub.
On a task page opened from the hub, the back link goes to the hub.

claims.statement: The main import reason (field importReason) offers five options, each with a hint: 'Internal market', 'Transhipment or onward travel', 'Transit', 'Re-entry' and 'Temporary admission horses'; none is selected on a fresh notification.
claims.quote:
Internal market
For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).
Transhipment or onward travel
For animals intended for direct travel to a third country, that will stay only within the same port or airport in Great Britain while moving to another means of transport.
Transit
For animals moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.
Re-entry
For animals authorised for re-entry, or rejected exports re-entering Great Britain.
Temporary admission horses
For horses authorised for temporary entry.
claims.note: Recorded here as the page reached from the hub; the reason page's own part owns its full detail.

claims.statement: The Main import reason page holds a hidden MOJ date picker for a temporary admission exit date, so choosing 'Temporary admission horses' presumably reveals an exit date question.

claims.statement: The review page ends with a 'Continue' submit button that posts to /design-release-2.1/review-notification.
Beside Continue, a red warning 'Delete' button links to /design-release-2.1/notifications/delete with the notification reference.
claims.quote: Delete

claims.statement: Pressing Continue on a review with incomplete tasks keeps the user on the review page, re-rendered with the same error summary, and does not move on to the declaration.

The review page's cards are custom app-dr2-review-card markup (a card header with a title and Change link, then a dl of rows), not the GOV.UK Summary list card; the Summary list with a card title and actions could replace it.
Opening /design-release-2.1/notification-submitted before the declaration is confirmed redirects to /design-release-2.1/declaration.
The submitted-page guard checks only the declaration, not task completeness: a brand-new notification with every task still to do is sent to the declaration, not to the review page.
claims.note: Inferred from the redirect target on a notification with nothing answered.

claims.statement: The declaration page's title is 'Declaration - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and its heading is 'Declaration'.
claims.quote: Declaration - Import notification service - GOV.UK || Declaration

claims.statement: The declaration page's back link goes to the review page.
The declaration page does not show the Draft tag or the notification reference.
claims.note: The quote is the eval result for the .app-dr2-notification-status lookup.

claims.statement: The declaration's first statement is about being the contact for the authorities and complying with Regulation (EU) 2017/625.
claims.quote:
I am the contact for the authorities and located in the UK.
I am complying with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 including on animal health and welfare.

claims.statement: The declaration's second statement is about responsibility for the consignment until it clears border checks or reaches its place of destination.
claims.quote:
I confirm I am responsible for this consignment.
I am responsible from the submission of this notification to when it enters Great Britain. And I am responsible until it has either:
cleared official checks at the border
reached the Place of Destination as stated on the health certificate or notification

claims.statement: The declaration's third statement lists the costs and arrangements the user is accountable for, and their authority to act for a third party.
claims.quote:
I confirm that I am accountable for:
any payment for the official controls at the border
any arrangements to re-dispatch the consignment
any costs needed for quarantine or isolation of consignments
any costs needed for destruction and disposal of consignments, when instructed by the authorities
I am authorised as being accountable for these things if raising notifications on behalf of a third party.
I can legally act on behalf of a third party in relation to the conditions of this declaration.

claims.statement: The declaration asks the user to tick a single small checkbox (field declarationConfirmed, value yes), unticked by default, inside a fieldset with the visually hidden legend 'Declaration confirmation'.
The declaration checkbox label reads: 'I confirm that I have reviewed and comply with this declaration and that the information submitted in this notification is true and correct.'
claims.quote: I confirm that I have reviewed and comply with this declaration and that the information submitted in this notification is true and correct.

claims.statement: The declaration page shows today's date as the date of declaration.
claims.note: Inferred as today's date because the trace ran on 7 October 2026.

claims.statement: The declaration page has a 'Continue' button that posts the form to /design-release-2.1/declaration.
The declaration page uses a two-thirds column with custom app-declaration-page section markup around standard GOV.UK checkboxes, bullet lists and button.

The hub, task pages and review are served by a GOV.UK Prototype Kit app with no data calls to other services: every answer is a form post to the prototype, and state is held in the prototype's session.
claims.note: Inferred from the network logs of all four traces showing only page loads, form posts, static assets and the kit's browser-sync socket. The session cookie value is redacted.

claims.statement: No trace in this slice shows a task in any state other than 'To do' or 'Complete', such as 'In progress' after a partial answer.
claims.ref: journeys.fit.spec.js › the notification hub (all four traces)

claims.statement: No trace in this slice presses 'Save and return to overview', so where it goes and whether it saves a partial answer are not shown.
No trace in this slice clicks 'Review and submit' or 'Return to dashboard' on the hub; only their link targets are seen.
No trace in this slice shows the commodities cards with non-zero totals, so how animal and package totals are counted is not shown.
No trace in this slice follows the review's Delete button, so the delete confirmation and its outcome are not shown.
No trace in this slice submits the declaration with the box unticked, so its validation error copy is not shown here.
No trace in this slice reaches the notification-submitted page itself, so its content once the declaration is confirmed is not shown here.
The hub is shown only for a live-animals notification in this slice; whether other notification types get the same sections and tasks is not shown.
claims.ref: journeys.fit.spec.js › the notification hub (all four traces start with notificationType live-animals)
